title: New Rules for AI Success: A Sneak Peek at the 2027 C-suite Imperatives Report
summary: Explore 5 insights from nearly 4,300 C-suite leaders on enterprise AI strategy, readiness, ERP modernization & driving measurable business value.
body_markdown:
AI has evolved, and so has the conversation around it. Leaders are no longer debating whether AI belongs in the enterprise. Instead, they’re asking:


- *How do we turn AI investments into measurable business value?*
- *In what area of the business should we introduce AI first?*
- *What separates successful AI initiatives from expensive experiments?*


The good news is that leaders don’t have to look far to find the answers.


Rimini Street conducts an annual C-suite research study to better understand the priorities, challenges and opportunities shaping business and technology strategy. This year, we partnered with Censuswide Research to survey nearly 4,300 CEOs, CFOs, CIOs and CISOs worldwide, focusing on one of today’s most pressing topics: AI.


The result is our upcoming 2027 C-suite Imperatives report, which explores how organizations are approaching AI strategy, readiness, modernization and business outcomes.


## 5 findings that could change your AI strategy


Before the full report launches, here’s a preview of what our survey uncovered.


### 1. Confidence is high, but reality is more complicated


Most leaders see tremendous potential in AI, and the overall outlook remains optimistic. Yet many organizations are still early in their AI journey, with pilots, proofs of concept and isolated use cases outpacing scalable business outcomes.


The lesson? Organizations that establish a clear path to execution and set realistic expectations from the get-go are better positioned to move from experimentation to measurable business value.


### 2. Technology isn’t the biggest barrier


Many organizations assume AI adoption is primarily a technology challenge. But our research suggests otherwise.


The biggest obstacles often involve governance, operational readiness, accountability and organizational alignment. In other words, the hardest part of AI may not be implementing it but preparing the business to use it effectively.


### 3. The C-suite isn’t always on the same page


Our research suggests that AI ownership is still a challenge for many organizations. Though AI is a shared priority among C-suite executives, they often have differing perspectives on accountability and long-term direction.


As AI decisions increasingly influence business strategy, organizations will need stronger alignment among finance, technology, security and executive leadership. Without it, even the most promising initiatives can struggle to gain momentum.


### 4. Business leaders are challenging the migration narrative


For years, many organizations have treated large-scale ERP migration projects as the default path to innovation.


Today’s leaders are starting to push back. Rather than assuming major platform changes are the only (or even the best) path forward, many are exploring how to innovate faster while maximizing existing technology investments.


### 5. The ROI reckoning has arrived


Adopting AI just for AI’s sake isn’t enough. The pressure to demonstrate a return is steadily growing.


Executives are focusing on measuring impact, prioritizing investments and determining where resources can generate the greatest business value. AI initiatives now face the same standard as any other investment: results.


## Why every leader should read this report


The next phase of enterprise AI will reward leaders who can align strategy, modernization and investment around measurable results. This report provides valuable insights into what that requires and how organizations are approaching the challenge today.
